transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I have this intense, over-the-top fear of being up high in tall buildings that doesn’t match what I know is the actual risk, and it’s starting to interfere with my work. I'm hoping to get some help with managing it.
Are you afraid only of tall buildings, or do you also feel anxious in other situations like open spaces, crowds, or public transportation?

No, I don't get anxious in crowds, open spaces, or on public transit at all. My fear is strictly focused on heights, like being high up in tall buildings, using glass elevators, or encountering exposed viewpoints when I'm hiking. Outside of those situations involving heights, I feel completely fine.
When you're in a high place, like a tall building or glass elevator, do you experience physical symptoms like dizziness, rapid heartbeat, or feeling like you might fall or lose control?

Yes, absolutely. My heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel really lightheaded even just picturing the elevator ride or being near those high windows. I also get these terrifying, irrational thoughts that the floor is going to give way or that I'll somehow get pulled right toward the glass.
